title: Sony Pictures Announces Global Release Date for Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana Epic
text:
A sweeping two-part cinematic adaptation of the Ramayana saga featuring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, scheduled for a global launch on November 6 with music by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.
The cinematic world is bracing for one of the most ambitious projects in Indian film history as Sony Pictures Entertainment officially unveils its plans for the global launch of Ramayana.
Scheduled to hit screens on November 6, this sweeping adaptation is not merely a movie but a cultural event designed to translate an ancient epic for a modern, global audience. Directed by the visionary Nitesh Tiwari, who previously achieved record-breaking success with Dangal, the film seeks to blend traditional storytelling with cutting-edge technology. The cast is equally prestigious, featuring Ranbir Kapoor in the pivotal role of the exiled prince Rama, whose journey represents the pinnacle of righteousness and duty.
Joining him is Sai Pallavi as the resilient and graceful Sita, while the powerhouse performer Yash takes on the formidable role of the demon king Ravana, providing a complex and imposing antagonist to drive the narrative forward. The story itself is a timeless exploration of love, loss, and the eternal struggle between good and evil. It follows the tragic exile of Rama and Sita, which culminates in a catastrophic turn of events when Ravana abducts Sita to his kingdom.
This act of aggression sets off a chain of events leading to an epic war that spans across three worlds, testing the limits of loyalty and courage. The timing of the release is deeply symbolic, as it coincides with Diwali, the festival of lights. This celebration commemorates Rama's triumphant return to Ayodhya after fourteen years of hardship and his ultimate victory over the forces of darkness.
The act of lighting lamps during Diwali serves as a poignant mirror to the film's themes, representing the illumination of hope and the return of a rightful leader to his people. This grand narrative will be unfolded across two parts, with the second installment planned for a Diwali release in 2027. From a technical standpoint, the production is nothing short of a spectacle.
To ensure the visual grandeur matches the scale of the mythology, the production team has enlisted DNEG, the eight-time Oscar-winning VFX house famous for its work on 'Interstellar' and 'Dune'. This ensures that the mythological weaponry and massive battle sequences described in the trailer will be rendered with stunning realism. The auditory experience is expected to be equally legendary, with Oscar winners Hans Zimmer and A.R.
Rahman collaborating to create a score that blends global cinematic textures with traditional Indian sounds. Further adding to the prestige are Terry Notary and Guy Norris, who are overseeing the action choreography, alongside Ramsey Avery and Ravi Bansal in the production design department. The film is being produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, with Sony handling the global rollout and Karan Johar's Dharma Productions managing the release within India.
Filmed specifically for IMAX presentation, the project aims to immerse viewers in a world of divine architecture and otherworldly landscapes. By offering the film in multiple languages, including English, Nitesh Tiwari and his team hope to make the 5,000-year-old saga accessible to people of all cultures, bridging the gap between ancient Eastern wisdom and contemporary Western cinema.
The screenplay, penned by Shridhar Raghavan, focuses on making the emotional core of the story resonate with audiences regardless of their familiarity with the source material. This project represents a significant leap in how mythological stories are presented on the world stage, promising an unprecedented cinematic experience that celebrates the richness of human emotion and the timeless nature of virtue
